judge.reason: Both versions behave the same. Each returns everything after a case-insensitive "bearer " prefix in HTTP_AUTHORIZATION, and nil when the header is missing or uses a different scheme. In Ruby, X's /m flag lets . match newlines, so X captures the whole rest of the value, just as Y's header[7, 100000000] does. Y is more complicated without gaining anything. It picks between match? and match by Ruby version (METHOD) and calls it through send. It checks the prefix twice, once in bearer_token and again in a private helper. It uses an arbitrary length constant. It also leaves a stray '#' line and a g
